title: Job, Chapter 8 (Leningrad Codex)
source: Leningrad Codex folios (Internet Archive, WSRP photographs) + tanach.us LC folio index + UXLC Hebrew + KJV
description: Job 8 on folios 399r, 399v of the Leningrad Codex (1008 AD), the oldest complete Hebrew Bible. Hebrew from the UXLC transcription of this manuscript; English KJV.
introduction:
Job chapter 8 from the Leningrad Codex (Codex Leningradensis, National Library of Russia, Firkovich EBP. I B 19a), copied in Cairo by Samuel ben Jacob and dated 1008/1009 AD, the oldest complete manuscript of the Hebrew Bible and the base text of the Biblia Hebraica editions. This chapter stands on folios 399r, 399v.

This entry meets the strict three-criteria standard of the Theosis Library:

  1. Manuscript scan: the specific folio side(s) carrying each section's verses, from the full-colour West Semitic Research Project photographs of the codex as redistributed on Internet Archive (item Leningrad_Codex_Color_Images, marked Creative Commons Public Domain Mark 1.0). Folio-to-verse ranges come from the tanach.us LC folio index, which was derived from the West Semitic Research Project's published index; each section links only to the page(s) whose recorded verse range contains its verses.
  2. Original text: the verbatim Hebrew of this manuscript in the Unicode/XML Leningrad Codex (UXLC 2.5 build 27.6, tanach.us), a transcription of Firkovich B 19a with vowels and cantillation, released without restriction on the biblical text.
  3. English translation: the King James Version (1611, public domain), retrieved verbatim from bolls.life (KJV text, Strong's numbers stripped).
translator_notes: פ and ס mark the open and closed paragraph breaks visible as gaps in the manuscript columns.

translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>וַ֭יַּעַן בִּלְדַּ֥ד הַשּׁוּחִ֗י וַיֹאמַֽר׃ <sup>2</sup>עַד־אָ֥ן תְּמַלֶּל־אֵ֑לֶּה וְר֥וּחַ כַּ֝בִּיר אִמְרֵי־פִֽיךָ׃ <sup>3</sup>הַ֭אֵל יְעַוֵּ֣ת מִשְׁפָּ֑ט וְאִם־שַׁ֝דַּ֗י יְעַוֵּֽת־צֶֽדֶק׃ <sup>4</sup>אִם־בָּנֶ֥יךָ חָֽטְאוּ־ל֑וֹ וַֽ֝יְשַׁלְּחֵ֗ם בְּיַד־פִּשְׁעָֽם׃ <sup>5</sup>אִם־אַ֭תָּה תְּשַׁחֵ֣ר אֶל־אֵ֑ל וְאֶל־שַׁ֝דַּ֗י תִּתְחַנָּֽן׃ <sup>6</sup>אִם־זַ֥ךְ וְיָשָׁ֗ר אָ֥תָּה כִּי־עַ֭תָּה יָעִ֣יר עָלֶ֑יךָ וְ֝שִׁלַּ֗ם נְוַ֣ת צִדְקֶֽךָ׃ <sup>7</sup>וְהָיָ֣ה רֵאשִׁיתְךָ֣ מִצְעָ֑ר וְּ֝אַחֲרִיתְךָ֗ יִשְׂגֶּ֥ה מְאֹֽד׃ <sup>8</sup>כִּֽי־שְׁאַל־נָ֭א לְדֹ֣ר רִישׁ֑וֹן וְ֝כוֹנֵ֗ן לְחֵ֣קֶר אֲבוֹתָֽם׃
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>Then answered Bildad the Shuhite, and said, <sup>2</sup>How long wilt thou speak these things? and how long shall the words of thy mouth be like a strong wind? <sup>3</sup>Doth God pervert judgment? or doth the Almighty pervert justice? <sup>4</sup>If thy children have sinned against him, and he have cast them away for their transgression; <sup>5</sup>If thou wouldest seek unto God betimes, and make thy supplication to the Almighty; <sup>6</sup>If thou wert pure and upright; surely now he would awake for thee, and make the habitation of thy righteousness prosperous. <sup>7</sup>Though thy beginning was small, yet thy latter end should greatly increase. <sup>8</sup>For enquire, I pray thee, of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers:

translation.original_text: <sup>9</sup>כִּֽי־תְמ֣וֹל אֲ֭נַחְנוּ וְלֹ֣א נֵדָ֑ע כִּ֤י צֵ֖ל יָמֵ֣ינוּ עֲלֵי־אָֽרֶץ׃ <sup>10</sup>הֲלֹא־הֵ֣ם י֭וֹרוּךָ יֹ֣אמְרוּ לָ֑ךְ וּ֝מִלִּבָּ֗ם יוֹצִ֥אוּ מִלִּֽים׃ <sup>11</sup>הֲיִֽגְאֶה־גֹּ֭מֶא בְּלֹ֣א בִצָּ֑ה יִשְׂגֶּה־אָ֥חוּ בְלִי־מָֽיִם׃ <sup>12</sup>עֹדֶ֣נּוּ בְ֭אִבּוֹ לֹ֣א יִקָּטֵ֑ף וְלִפְנֵ֖י כָל־חָצִ֣יר יִיבָֽשׁ׃ <sup>13</sup>כֵּ֗ן אָ֭רְחוֹת כָּל־שֹׁ֣כְחֵי אֵ֑ל וְתִקְוַ֖ת חָנֵ֣ף תֹּאבֵֽד׃ <sup>14</sup>אֲשֶׁר־יָק֥וֹט כִּסְל֑וֹ וּבֵ֥ית עַ֝כָּבִישׁ מִבְטַחֽוֹ׃ <sup>15</sup>יִשָּׁעֵ֣ן עַל־בֵּ֭יתוֹ וְלֹ֣א יַעֲמֹ֑ד יַחֲזִ֥יק בּ֝֗וֹ וְלֹ֣א יָקֽוּם׃ <sup>16</sup>רָטֹ֣ב ה֭וּא לִפְנֵי־שָׁ֑מֶשׁ וְעַ֥ל גַּ֝נָּת֗וֹ יֹ֭נַקְתּ֥וֹ תֵצֵֽא׃
translation.text: <sup>9</sup>(For we are but of yesterday, and know nothing, because our days upon earth are a shadow:) <sup>10</sup>Shall not they teach thee, and tell thee, and utter words out of their heart? <sup>11</sup>Can the rush grow up without mire? can the flag grow without water? <sup>12</sup>Whilst it is yet in his greenness, and not cut down, it withereth before any other herb. <sup>13</sup>So are the paths of all that forget God; and the hypocrite's hope shall perish: <sup>14</sup>Whose hope shall be cut off, and whose trust shall be a spider's web. <sup>15</sup>He shall lean upon his house, but it shall not stand: he shall hold it fast, but it shall not endure. <sup>16</sup>He is green before the sun, and his branch shooteth forth in his garden.

translation.original_text: <sup>17</sup>עַל־גַּ֭ל שָֽׁרָשָׁ֣יו יְסֻבָּ֑כוּ בֵּ֖ית אֲבָנִ֣ים יֶחֱזֶֽה׃ <sup>18</sup>אִם־יְבַלְּעֶ֥נּוּ מִמְּקוֹמ֑וֹ וְכִ֥חֶשׁ בּ֝֗וֹ לֹ֣א רְאִיתִֽיךָ׃ <sup>19</sup>הֶן־ה֭וּא מְשׂ֣וֹשׂ דַּרְכּ֑וֹ וּ֝מֵעָפָ֗ר אַחֵ֥ר יִצְמָֽחוּ׃ <sup>20</sup>הֶן־אֵ֭ל לֹ֣א יִמְאַס־תָּ֑ם וְלֹֽא־יַ֝חֲזִ֗יק בְּיַד־מְרֵעִֽים׃ <sup>21</sup>עַד־יְמַלֵּ֣ה שְׂח֣וֹק פִּ֑יךָ וּשְׂפָתֶ֥יךָ תְרוּעָֽה׃ <sup>22</sup>שֹׂנְאֶ֥יךָ יִלְבְּשׁוּ־בֹ֑שֶׁת וְאֹ֖הֶל רְשָׁעִ֣ים אֵינֶֽנּוּ׃ פ
translation.text: <sup>17</sup>His roots are wrapped about the heap, and seeth the place of stones. <sup>18</sup>If he destroy him from his place, then it shall deny him, saying, I have not seen thee. <sup>19</sup>Behold, this is the joy of his way, and out of the earth shall others grow. <sup>20</sup>Behold, God will not cast away a perfect man, neither will he help the evil doers: <sup>21</sup>Till he fill thy mouth with laughing, and thy lips with rejoicing. <sup>22</sup>They that hate thee shall be clothed with shame; and the dwelling place of the wicked shall come to nought.
